topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: A defocused reflector design offers improved robustness against feed element failures but at the cost of a 6 dB gain roll-off, which reduces the usable beamwidth and co-polar isolation, necessitating a higher SNR budget. Mitigating this trade-off through advanced beamforming techniques or additional feed elements can improve performance but increases complexity and cost. System designers must carefully balance these factors to ensure reliable operation in satellite communication systems.
